Each row: 10,000 draws of 10 runs out of 30, split into two groups of 5, at random or sorted by final score (generator \texttt{default\_rng(2018)}). Three readings of `the average t-test across the entire training curve': Welch $t$ at each point then averaged, turned into a $p$ with the mean degrees of freedom; mean of the $p$ values; the 5 runs $\times$ 20 points of each group stacked as 100 independent observations. Then the script \texttt{from\_same\_dist.py} Henderson published in 2017: a Welch test at each iteration on the standard deviation between the episodes of one point, mean of the $t$ and $p$ values; the spread between seeds never enters it. Columns: share of draws declared different ($p < 0.05$, false positives since both groups run the same code), 95th percentile of $|t|$, share of draws where $|t|$ reaches 9.09. Shares in percent rounded to the unit, to one significant digit below 1\%. \textbf{In bold}, the only rows where $|t|$ reaches 9.09: the 2017 script applied to TRPO, whose standard deviation between episodes is only 7\% of the standard deviation between seeds (PPO: 30\%). Coefficient of variation of the final scores: TRPO 48\%, PPO 34\%. Sources: \file{sim/analysis/b1\_trpo.json}, \file{sim/analysis/b1\_script.json} (the PPO mean-$t$ row repeats the computation of \file{sim/analysis/e1\_curve.json}).}
